source_snapshot.test_name: NVLink enumeration and full NVLink fabric topology (144 NVLinks between GPU and NVSwitch)
source_snapshot.items: NVLink enumeration and full NVLink fabric topology (144 NVLinks between GPU and NVSwitch)
source_snapshot.procedure: Use the latest NVDiag version to run FCT.
source_snapshot.criteria: The log should show pass except for SKU check, and the SUT should remain workable.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: Run an unspecified nvqual/nvlink `nvlink_topology` module and return its pass log; it additionally mentions long bandwidth/application tests not present in the source.

original_test_intent.purpose: Verify that every expected NVIDIA GPU, NVSwitch, port and GPU-to-switch NVLink in the exact platform fabric enumerates in the platform-defined topology, including the source-required total of 144 GPU links, and confirm post-test SUT usability.
original_test_intent.target: The complete single-node NVIDIA GPU/NVSwitch fabric for the identified HGX/DGX/ODM baseboard generation and SKU, correlated by stable GPU, switch and link/port identifiers.
original_test_intent.scope: Topology and link enumeration against an exact 144-link manifest; the case does not independently request NVLink bandwidth or application performance and those must not be added by inference.
original_test_intent.operation: Collect a generation-specific baseline, run the qualified vendor FCT topology profile, retain the full enumerated map and status, compare every manifest edge and endpoint, then recheck fabric/SUT health without clearing logs.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: One complete topology/FCT pass over the expected fabric; source timing is 10 attended and 20 machine minutes, with no bandwidth duration or repetition stated.
original_test_intent.expected_result: All expected GPUs, NVSwitches and 144 GPU-link edges are present, mapped to the correct generation-specific switch ports and healthy; only a precisely approved SKU-check exception may be ignored, and the SUT/fabric remains usable.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Exact platform/SKU/baseboard generation, NVDiag build/hash/profile, expected 144-edge manifest, stable GPU/switch/link IDs, complete FCT topology/status/exit output, independent pre/post fabric state and errors, bounded exception, timestamps, and concrete usability checks.
ambiguities: The platform generation/SKU is absent; multiple HGX generations can total 144 GPU links while using different NVSwitch counts and port mappings.
`latest NVDiag`, FCT profile/module/side effects and stable switch/link identifier mapping are undefined.
The source does not define whether 144 counts GPU-side links, switch-side ports, bidirectional directions, or another representation.
The SKU-check exception and workable criteria are unbounded.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly requires the package, exact inventory, a 144-link manifest, per-port mapping, side-effect review, isolation, complete topology/error evidence and recovery. It adopts DeepSeek's `nvlink_topology` module name without source proof and does not show why 144 alone is insufficient across NVIDIA baseboard generations.

applicable_history.decision: Vendor package and platform manifest are supplyable prerequisites; missing artifacts do not imply permanent BLOCKED, but no command or universal topology may be invented.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: V2's classification is retained. V3 makes the platform-generation decision mandatory because H100/H200-class and B200/B300-class baseboards can each expose 144 GPU links through different NVSwitch/port maps; count-only or GPU-index-only checks cannot prove full topology.

available_now: The full-fabric topology/enumeration intent, 144-link total, NVIDIA vendor FCT dependency and post-test usability goal are explicit.
Read-only GPU UUID/BDF, NVSwitch/fabric-manager inventory, link-state/topology and existing XID/NVSwitch/kernel/BMC evidence can be collected before the proprietary harness is supplied.
missing_inputs: Exact HGX/DGX/ODM baseboard generation/SKU and definition of the 144 counted edges
Owner-approved per-edge manifest mapping stable GPU/module/link IDs to NVSwitch IDs/ports, including applicable unused/reserved/degraded-port policy
Qualified NVDiag/nvqual build/hash/license, exact profile/module/command/config, supported driver/firmware/Fabric Manager or NVLSM state, side effects and result semantics
Bounded SKU-check exception, idle window, stop thresholds, concrete fabric/SUT usability checks, OOB recovery and approval
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The NVIDIA/platform qualification owner supplies platform identity, manifest, harness semantics and exception; the GPU/fabric and lab owners approve software compatibility, isolation, side effects, limits and recovery.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Collect GPU UUID/BDF/module identifiers, switch/Fabric Manager or NVLSM inventory and status, `nvidia-smi topo -m`/approved link status, driver/firmware versions and complete current topology
Capture XID, NVLink/NVSwitch health/error state, active jobs, kernel/BMC/SEL baseline and OOB reachability without clearing or resetting anything
prohibited_until_closed: Do not infer platform generation from the number 144, use GPU enumeration indices as stable IDs, invent an `nvlink_topology` command, select `latest`, or apply an H100 port map to B200/B300 or vice versa
Do not add bandwidth/application stress, ignore any SKU failure generically, clear logs, run an unreviewed diagnostic on active GPUs, or declare PASS from count alone
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: The owner signs a generation-specific edge manifest and count definition; package/profile documentation confirms targets, effects and output IDs; actual stable identities map one-to-one, exceptions are bounded, workloads drained, and OOB/stop/recovery checks approved.

revision_candidate.test_name: Generation-Specific 144-Link NVIDIA NVSwitch Fabric Topology Validation
revision_candidate.purpose: Verify the complete expected 144-edge GPU-to-NVSwitch fabric for the exact platform, including correct endpoint/port mapping and healthy enumeration, then confirm the fabric and SUT remain usable.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: One explicitly identified NVIDIA HGX/DGX/ODM baseboard generation and SKU with its qualified driver, GPU/NVSwitch firmware, Fabric Manager or NVLSM stack, approved NVDiag/nvqual build and OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every GPU and NVSwitch edge in the owner-approved 144-link manifest. The count and switch-port map are platform-specific; no NVLink bandwidth or application workload is included unless separately specified.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: Platform/SKU and count definition, stable GPU/switch/link identifiers, full edge manifest, unused/degraded policy, qualified package/profile/command/config and side effects, software/firmware matrix, bounded SKU exception, isolation/window, limits, usability checks, and recovery owner.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve an independent full-fabric baseline, run only the package-documented approved FCT topology profile, capture complete raw topology/status and exit results, compare every observed stable endpoint/port edge with the signed 144-edge manifest, then re-read fabric/error state and usability. Do not substitute an invented module or a count-only check.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Verified platform identity and manifest, compatible package/driver/firmware/fabric service, complete stable-ID mapping, idle GPUs, reviewed side effects, preserved evidence, approved exception/thresholds, synchronized timestamps and working OOB recovery.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Package/hash/profile/config; platform/SKU/count definition; expected and observed per-edge map; GPU UUID/BDF/module and NVSwitch/port identities; every link state; complete FCT output/exit status; exact exception; Fabric Manager/NVLSM and XID/NVSwitch/kernel/BMC deltas; cleanup and usability checks.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The exact platform generation's owner-approved GPU-to-NVSwitch edge manifest and the qualified FCT build's result semantics. The integer 144 is necessary but not sufficient evidence of correct topology.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: No cross-generation manifest, unstable GPU indices, unreviewed package/profile, active jobs, blanket exception, added traffic test, log clearing, autonomous reset/retrain, or continuation after fabric degradation, GPU/NVSwitch reset, XID or management impact.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Explicit approval is required for platform manifest, package/profile and effects, job drain, exception policy, diagnostic window, thresholds and recovery.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners provide proprietary harness and generation-specific topology truth; after approval, inventory, FCT launch, per-edge comparison and post-checks are automatable. Unmapped edges, vendor failures and recovery remain engineering decisions.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: Stop the harness, preserve full map and error evidence, verify no traffic/retrain process remains, re-enumerate all devices/links, use OOB on impact, and perform reset/restart/reboot only under the platform recovery procedure; quarantine unresolved fabric faults.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unknown platform/count definition, incomplete manifest, incompatible package/software, active jobs, identity collision, missing/miswired/down/degraded edge, unexpected unused port, GPU/NVSwitch reset, XID/fabric/kernel/BMC error, management loss, unapproved exception, incomplete output, or failed usability/recovery.

identified_defects: A 144-link total is not a topology proof because different NVIDIA baseboard generations can use different NVSwitch counts and port mappings while retaining 18 GPU links per GPU.
The proprietary FCT profile/command and exact platform are absent.
DeepSeek invents an `nvlink_topology` module and expands scope toward bandwidth/application testing.
The SKU exception and count representation are undefined.
reason_for_change: Make the 144 requirement testable as a generation-specific graph rather than a scalar count and prevent a fabricated module or extra performance workload from changing the source intent.

new_technical_evidence.title: NVIDIA Fabric Manager User Guide: NVLink Topology
new_technical_evidence.supports: The official GPU-link-to-NVSwitch-port maps differ by baseboard generation; HGX H100/H200 uses four NVSwitches with 18 links per GPU, while HGX B200/B300 uses two NVSwitches with nine links from each GPU to each switch, yielding the same 144 GPU-link total for eight GPUs but a different graph.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The testcase does not identify which platform/SKU or counting representation applies.

removed_ambiguities: Defines 144 as an owner-specified edge representation that must be documented.
Requires generation-specific per-port mapping, not a count or index-only comparison.
resolved_blockers: Missing harness and manifest are supplyable prerequisites; safe inventory and topology capture can proceed first.
remaining_blockers: FCT execution and acceptance await exact platform/count definition, per-edge manifest, qualified package/profile, exception, isolation, approval and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 adds official evidence that identical 144 totals can mask different H100/H200 versus B200/B300 graphs, removes DeepSeek's invented module/performance expansion, and makes per-edge comparison the completion criterion while retaining V2's classification and safety controls.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source explicitly requires full GPU-to-NVSwitch topology with 144 NVLinks using NVDiag FCT.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 requires a manifest; V3 proves count-only insufficiency across generations and removes the unverified module name and added performance scope.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Inventory safely first; run no harness until generation-specific graph, package semantics, exception, side effects and recovery are approved; never clear logs or accept count-only PASS.
